entries.name: Heritrix
entries.definition: An open-source, archival-quality web crawler developed by the Internet Archive.

entries.name: Higher education law
entries.definition: The body of law that governs colleges and universities, including student rights, accreditation, funding and employment.

entries.name: Higher education policy
entries.definition: The study and practice of the public and institutional rules, funding and governance that shape colleges and universities.

entries.name: HincII
entries.definition: A type II restriction enzyme, formerly named HindII, that cuts DNA at a specific six-base recognition sequence.

entries.name: HindIII
entries.definition: A type II restriction enzyme from Haemophilus influenzae that cuts DNA at the sequence AAGCTT.

entries.name: Hindsight bias
entries.definition: The tendency, after an outcome is known, to believe one would have predicted it.

entries.name: Historic preservation
entries.definition: The field of protecting and conserving historic buildings, sites and objects.

entries.name: Historical linguistics
entries.definition: The study of how languages change over time and how they are related to one another.

entries.name: History of education
entries.definition: The study of how education and schooling have developed over time.

entries.name: History of medicine
entries.definition: The study of how medical practice, knowledge and institutions have developed over time.

entries.name: History of philosophy
entries.definition: The study of how philosophical ideas and thinkers have developed over time.

entries.name: History of science
entries.definition: The study of how scientific ideas, methods and institutions have developed over time.

entries.name: Hockett's design features
entries.definition: A set of features proposed by the linguist Charles Hockett that characterise human language and set it apart from animal communication.

entries.name: Honeypot
entries.definition: A decoy system or resource set up to attract attackers so their methods can be detected and studied.

entries.name: Hootsuite
entries.definition: A social media management platform for scheduling posts, monitoring accounts and reporting on results.

entries.name: Host Based Security System
entries.definition: The US Department of Defense's endpoint security suite, built on McAfee ePolicy Orchestrator, for monitoring and protecting hosts.

entries.name: Hotel and restaurant management
entries.definition: Running the operations of hotels and restaurants, including staff, service, finances and guest satisfaction.

entries.name: Hotel management
entries.definition: Overseeing the daily operation of a hotel, including rooms, staff, finances and guest service.

entries.name: HotJava
entries.definition: A web browser written in Java by Sun Microsystems in the 1990s.

entries.name: HP 2100
entries.definition: A series of 16-bit minicomputers made by Hewlett-Packard from the 1960s.

entries.name: HP 9845C
entries.definition: A colour-display model of Hewlett-Packard's HP 9845 series of technical desktop computers.

entries.name: HP Application Lifecycle Management
entries.definition: HP's software suite for managing requirements, testing and defects across the life of a software application.

entries.name: HP Brio
entries.definition: A line of business desktop personal computers sold by Hewlett-Packard.

entries.name: HP Jornada
entries.definition: A line of Hewlett-Packard handheld computers and personal digital assistants running Windows CE.

entries.name: HP NewWave
entries.definition: A graphical, object-oriented desktop environment from Hewlett-Packard that ran on top of Microsoft Windows.

entries.name: HP Quality Center
entries.definition: A test management tool from HP, originally developed by Mercury Interactive, for managing requirements, test cases and defects.

entries.name: HP Systems Insight Manager
entries.definition: HP software for monitoring and managing HP servers, storage and network devices from one console.

entries.name: HP WinRunner
entries.definition: An automated functional testing tool, originally from Mercury Interactive, that records and replays user actions on graphical applications.

entries.name: HR analytics
entries.definition: Analysing workforce data to inform decisions about hiring, retention, pay and performance.

entries.name: HTML emails
entries.definition: Designing and coding email messages in HTML, allowing for the uneven way email clients display them.

entries.name: HTML formatting
entries.definition: Marking up and styling text and page content with HTML tags.

entries.name: html5shiv
entries.definition: A small JavaScript library that lets old versions of Internet Explorer recognise and style HTML5 elements.

entries.name: HubSpot CRM
entries.definition: HubSpot's customer relationship management software for tracking contacts, companies, deals and sales activity.

entries.name: Human capital management integration
entries.definition: Connecting human capital management software, which holds HR and payroll data, with other business systems so that data flows between them.

entries.name: Human factors
entries.definition: The study of how people interact with machines, systems and environments, used to make them safer, easier to use and more effective.

entries.name: Human factors engineering
entries.definition: Applying knowledge of human abilities and limits to design equipment, interfaces and tasks that are safe, usable and effective.

entries.name: Human-machine interface
entries.definition: The screens, controls and displays through which an operator monitors and controls a machine or industrial process.

entries.name: Human musculoskeletal system
entries.definition: The bones, muscles, joints and connective tissue that support the human body and let it move.

entries.name: Human rights law
entries.definition: The national and international laws that protect people's basic rights and freedoms.

entries.name: HVAC automation systems
entries.definition: Systems that automatically monitor and control heating, ventilation and air conditioning equipment in buildings.
